claims.quote: The mainstay of treatment is topical antimicrobials with or without topical corticosteroids.
The treatment of mild or moderate acute otitis externa consists of topical agents (primarily topical antimicrobials) for 7 to 10 days

claims.text: No clinical outcome difference between quinolone and non-quinolone drops, or with vs without a steroid
claims.quote: There are no significant clinical outcome differences between the drug classes, quinolone vs. nonquinolone antibiotics, or preparations with or without corticosteroids.

claims.text: Mild: 2% acetic acid (lowers canal pH) + hydrocortisone, 5 drops TID for 7 days
claims.quote: Mild external otitis can be treated by altering the ear canal's pH with 2% acetic acid (or white vinegar) and by relieving inflammation with topical hydrocortisone; these are given as 5 drops 3 times a day for 7 days.

claims.text: Moderate: add ciprofloxacin or ofloxacin drops;
claims.quote: Moderate external otitis requires the addition of an antibacterial solution or suspension, such as ciprofloxacin or ofloxacin.
In mild or moderate acute external otitis, topical antibiotics and glucocorticoids are effective (eg, ciprofloxacin and fluocinolone)

claims.text: Perforated TM: ciprofloxacin/dexamethasone (Ciprodex) and ofloxacin 0.3% may be used; acetic acid, ciprofloxacin/hydrocortisone, hydrocortisone/acetic acid and neomycin/polymyxin B/hydrocortisone may not.

claims.text: Avoid potentially ototoxic drops (aminoglycosides, isopropyl alcohol)
claims.quote: If a perforation or suspected perforation of the tympanic membrane has occurred, topical medications that are potentially ototoxic (e.g., aminoglycosides, isopropyl alcohol) should not be used;

claims.text: Neomycin/polymyxin: MSD says it is no longer recommended (neomycin sensitizes up to 13% of pts and is ototoxic with a TM perforation).
claims.quote: Neomycin/polymyxin is no longer recommended because the neomycin component is highly sensitizing and causes an allergic reaction in up to 13% of patients (5). In addition, neomycin is ototoxic and risks injury to the inner ear and permanent hearing loss in the presence of a tympanic membrane perforation.

claims.text: Severe canal swelling: an ear wick wetted with Burow solution or an antibiotic drop QID,
claims.quote: When inflammation and swelling of the ear canal are relatively severe, an ear wick should be placed into the ear canal and wetted with Burow solution (5% aluminum acetate) or a topical antibiotic 4 times a day.
The wick is left in place for 24 to 72 hours

claims.text: Fungal OE: antimycotic solution (eg, nystatin, clotrimazole, acetic acid + isopropyl alcohol) after cleaning; not with a perforated TM
claims.quote: Fungal external otitis requires thorough cleaning of the ear canal and application of an antimycotic solution (eg, gentian violet, cresylate acetate, nystatin, clotrimazole, or even a combination of acetic acid and isopropyl alcohol). However, these solutions should not be used if the tympanic membrane is perforated

claims.text: Otic benzocaine (± antipyrine) was withdrawn from the US market in 2015
claims.quote: The use of otic benzocaine with or without antipyrine was withdrawn from the U.S. market in 2015.
